historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.4 TDCi (Puma) launched in the Defender 90, it marked Land Rover's transition to Ford-sourced Duratorq diesel engines, offering improved refinement and emissions compliance over the outgoing TD5.

milestones.description: 244DT (2.4L TDCi), 122hp, introduced with the distinctive "Puma" bonnet update to meet Euro 4 emissions standards.
Facelift to the 2.2L TDCi (DT224) for Euro 5 compliance, concluding the 2.4 TDCi production run for the classic Defender 90.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi (244DT) is generally robust, but Puma-era engines are prone to specific turbo and emissions system failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbo Wastegate Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi 244DT Loses Boost
problems.rootCause: The vacuum-operated wastegate solenoid and associated vacuum lines degrade over time, causing the turbo to default to a safe, low-boost state.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the faulty solenoid and checking vacuum lines for leaks.
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before secondary turbo damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the turbo failure has caused secondary engine damage or if the engine already has high mileage.

problems.recommendation: For the Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi, if the issue is isolated to the wastegate solenoid or EGR, a specialist repair is highly cost-effective. However, if you are experiencing concurrent issues (e.g., turbo failure combined with high oil consumption or timing chain noise), a reconditioned engine with upgraded components is the safest long-term solution.

problems.h4: EGR Valve Fouling - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi 244DT Enters Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: Carbon buildup from the exhaust gas recirculation system restricts airflow, triggering engine management warnings and severe power restriction.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical cleaning of the EGR valve and intake manifold, or fitting an EGR blanking plate (where legally permissible).
repairOptions.longevity: Good temporary fix, but carbon buildup may recur in urban driving conditions.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if severe carbon ingestion has damaged valves or the turbo.

items.question: What are the signs of turbo failure in a Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi?
items.answer: The most common early warning sign is a sudden loss of power or the vehicle entering "limp mode" under acceleration.
keyPoints: You may also hear unusual whining or whistling noises from the engine bay.
Excessive blue or grey smoke from the exhaust often accompanies these symptoms.
Dashboard warning lights, particularly the engine management light, will typically illuminate.
items.cta: -> Get a diagnostic quote for your Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi?
items.answer: Yes, given the strong retained value of classic Defender 90 models (typically £8,000-£18,000), a rebuild is often financially viable.
keyPoints: A reconditioned 244DT engine with a 12-month warranty restores reliability and protects your asset's value.
Always compare the replacement cost against the current market value of your specific vehicle's condition.
items.cta: -> Check if your Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi is a candidate for replacement.

items.question: How long does a Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi engine replacement take?
items.answer: A professional supply and fit service for the Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi typically takes 2 to 3 days.
keyPoints: This includes the removal of the old 244DT unit and thorough engine bay cleaning.
Installation of the replacement and comprehensive post-fit testing are completed before handover.
Nationwide mobile fitting services can often complete this at your home or workplace.
items.cta: -> Book a Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi supply and fit appointment.

items.question: Can I upgrade my Land Rover Defender 90 2.4 TDCi to a newer engine?
items.answer: While the 2.2 TDCi (DT224) is the direct successor, swapping engine management systems and wiring looms between Puma generations is complex.
keyPoints: Such modifications may affect MOT emissions compliance and require extensive custom fabrication.
The most reliable and legally compliant route is to replace the 244DT with a like-for-like reconditioned unit featuring preventative upgrades.
